mission.title: Seance
mission.description: Track down the Machine program that tended Mary MacHenry's pod, and find out what the Machines did with her.

npc.say: You had best be going, mon ami. The Machines may decide to terminate that program now that it has been "soiled" by contact with our dangerous band of rebels, mm?

As I feared... The Trainman's continued absence leaves us without a means of bringing the program here, into our power.
No... I do not know. There has been no sighting of him since he fled from the Machines into his private subway network. The Machines have been seen to have continued searching for him. He could be dead.
I felt I was a slave then, but at least I touched...real people. Now all I have is this...this grand illusion.
It is strange...but it reminds me of something... Something that happened long ago. I did not understand it then, but now...
To use her as some sort of operative, perhaps?

phase.briefing:
The sad saga of Mary MacHenry continues, operative. It seems that for some reason, the Machines saw fit to remove her "real" body from her pod--not by flushing her into the sewers from whence all you operatives sprang, but by carefully prizing her out through the gummy seal on top of the pod.
Unfortunate for us that they did not simply send her swirling down the drain, because we're now tasked with finding just what they were doing with her; not that anyone in our organization cares about her personally, I hope, but it is odd for the Machines to be ferrying humans around on the surface of your mudball planet like that.
The General already helped find which pod was hers. Now we're going to track down the Machine caretaker program that handled her in her pod; Persephone used to have a similar function, so we know more or less how to look this up. You just have to rub out any Machines that get in your way.

enter.say: You've just got to secure a terminal in there, and we can do the rest. I'm reading some Machine programs marching around inside, so watch yourself.

I'm getting a promising data signature near your location. Do you see a computer terminal?
Whoops, heads up. More Machine signals just appeared up on my monitor.

objective.text: Get the data from the terminal

done.say:
There's the data!
Jeez, better get it, quick; I've got more Machines incoming. New signals are popping up like rabbits...

objective.text: Upload the data at a hardline

phase.briefing:
Right... Now, if the Trainman hadn't got himself cut to ribbons by Machines, we could simply nip into Machine city and grab the program that data identified as the caretaker of MacHenry's pod. As it is, we'll have to settle for hijacking it remotely long enough to get some information out of it.
Get there quickly, please, {player}. There's no telling what trouble the Effectuator will get into if he's left unsupervised for any appreciable amount of time.

enter.say: The Effectuator's in there. Hey...so are Malphas, the Merv, and Persephone.

talk.say:
Oh, hey. That data you got told us which Machine program was taking care of Mary's pod. It's...um...a little inconvenient to bring them into the Matrix right now, so we're going to try hijacking them remotely for a bit, just to talk. In fact, I think they're coming through right now...
Hm? Oh. In the body of that blood-drinker, of course.

done.say:
Subroutine 000c8201-DMT3R, we seek information on the human recently removed from pod 0100:021:0257:084. The sooner you tell us what we wish to know, the sooner you can return to your duties.
Why was the human removed?
A good old-fashioned soul-summoning, huh? The "possessed" vamp there doesn't seem too impressed.

talk.say: Fallen Programs. I Have Nothing To Say To You. You Cannot Hold Me.

done.say:
Smoo-ooth.
Well, that didn't go so great... Where's that leave us?
Ooh... Yeah. I think we lost it.

talk.say:
Hm... Those mothering programs are so defensive...eh, Persephone?
No matter... We know that it is still active. The Machines will have records of its activity; we will simply have to take what they would not give willingly. Flood will direct you.

phase.briefing:
Somehow we always end up having to do things the hard way when you're around, {player}. I wonder why that is, hm?
Now you'll have to use a particular Machine terminal to access that caretaker program's activity history.
Oh, yes, I suppose they'll try and stop you. That's your affair.

enter.say: I'm reading a lot of program activity in there. It's not gonna be easy to get in and out without being seen.

objective.text: Get the activity history from the Machine terminal

done.say: Okay, that should be the data we need.
Plug that into a hardline for me.

objective.text: Upload the activity history at a hardline

phase.briefing: It isn't my job to interpret that gobbledygook. There are people who do that sort of thing for me.

enter.say: That's your rendezvous point. No hostiles in sight.

talk.say: That data shows that the woman in the pod was put through physical conditioning just before she was removed. They worked her muscles very heavily... But why?

Curious. We know of no use the Machines have for physically active humans--indeed, their attitude is usually one of disdain for your bodies as anything other than a passive energy source. But the effort they put into Mrs. MacHenry before unplugging her suggests that they were not simply going to kill her. They wanted her able to function in the outer world.

mission.finish:
Yes... Machine efficiency at its finest, I'm sure. Apparently the pod-dwellers can now request personal massage therapy.
Did it ever occur to you, {player}, that maybe MacHenry was in first class, while you flew in coach?
